Sophie - Partnerships: FYI CloudWave flagged ~1.9% delta between their reported consumed_units and our ingested usage for the window 2026-03-13 -> 2026-03-19. They say multiple late batches arrived after 00:00 UTC which got assigned to the previous day's rollup on their side. sample payloads: s3://redwood-partners/cloudwave/samples/cw-sample-20260319.csv :eyes:

Marketplace Bot: webhook cw-evt-33421 delivered 2026-03-20T00:08:12Z -> 200 OK (ack_id=ack-77c2). Delivery latency=8m12s.

Maya P: can you drop one of the sample event IDs? I want to check how our aggregator assigned the event timestamp vs their claim. quick sanity check: did the webhook include downstream timestamp or only event_created_at? :thinking:

Sophie - Partnerships: listed in the CSV: cw-evt-33421, cw-evt-33422, cw-evt-33457. CloudWave says cw-evt-33421 and cw-evt-33422 were generated at 2026-03-19T23:58:xxZ but delivered after midnight due to their batching pipeline.

Leo Chen: likely this is the classic "generation_ts vs ingestion_ts" mismatch. Our rollup key uses event_hour aligned to ingestion_timezone (UTC) when the message is processed by the connector. If they expect generator_time to determine day boundary we need to reconcile.

Diego (SI): on CloudWave side they use device_local_time -> convert -> batch -> send. They admit batching delay up to 15m during heavy runs. They included a CSV with two fields: generator_ts and delivered_at.

Maya P: quick query to inspect how these were stored in the hourly rollup table:

```
-- find event assignment
select event_id, generator_ts, delivered_at, rollup_day, rollup_hour
from partner_hourly_rollups
where partner = 'cloudwave' and event_id in ('cw-evt-33421','cw-evt-33422');
```

Maya P: If rollup_hour is NULL or the delivered_at is used we should see mismatches. Also check our dedupe window — if they replayed late, we might have de-duplicated or overwritten previous entries.

Ana Ops: I'll check ingestion logs and the connector checkpointing. Two things to validate: 1) how the connector sets the effective_timestamp (generator_ts vs delivered_at), and 2) if our backfill job applied a last-writer-wins policy that could have moved units between days. Running a quick grep on the connector config: `connector.config.use_generator_ts=true` or false.

Marketplace Bot: Backfill job job-rlb-20260320 started 2026-03-20T01:12:03Z, targeting partner=cloudwave, window=2026-03-13..2026-03-19, status=running.

Diego (SI): CloudWave suggested we prefer generator_ts for attribution. They can add a field `attribution_time` in their next payloads. Is that safe for our ingestion? Any side effects on billing if we switch attribution anchor?

Leo Chen: switching anchors changes charge day attribution — billing contracts must reflect that. Short-term: we can implement a reconciliation mapping that attributes units back to generator_ts for partner-reported claims only (not modifying canonical billing until legal sign-off). I propose: create a reconciliation delta report that shows per-day consumed_units_by_ingestion vs consumed_units_by_generator for the disputed window. Example query:

```
-- reconciliation delta
select day,
  sum(ingested_units) as ingested_units,
  sum(case when generator_ts::date = day then units else 0 end) as gen_attributed_units,
  sum(ingested_units) - sum(case when generator_ts::date = day then units else 0 end) as delta
from partner_usage_events
where partner='cloudwave' and event_date between '2026-03-13' and '2026-03-19'
group by day
order by day;
```

Maya P: I can run that once Ana confirms which fields exist on the stored events. If delta == ~1.9% we can generate a per-invoice draft adjustment for partner review.

Sophie - Partnerships: CloudWave asked for quick mitigation: 1) can we provide a per-day delta report so they can reconcile on their side, 2) can we add a flag to our partner portal indicating "late-delivery attribution pending" so partners see which events are under dispute?

Ana Ops: I'll produce the delta report — running now. ETA 30m. Also creating a Trello ticket to track anchor-change requests. If we need to change canonical billing attribution we'll need approvals from finance and legal.

Diego (SI): FYI on CloudWave's side they can optionally send `original_day` field in payload. That would make reconciliation straightforward. We should support that as a non-breaking attribute that only affects reporting until policy is updated.

Maya P: for the immediate triage, please include: sample event payload (full JSON), connector logs around processing of cw-evt-33421, and the backfill job logs. Put them in the shared folder and ping here when uploaded.

Sophie - Partnerships: uploaded CSV + sample JSONs to s3://redwood-partners/cloudwave/triage/1768002345/ — notifying CloudWave that we're running the delta report. :thumbsup:

Marketplace Bot: delta-report (job-id=delta-1768002400) completed 2026-03-20T00:52:40Z. Summary: total ingested units=124,312; generator-attributed units=126,725; net delta = +2,413 (1.94%) skewed to day 2026-03-19. Full CSV at s3://redwood-partners/cloudwave/triage/1768002345/delta.csv

Sophie - Partnerships: sharing results with CloudWave. They'll take a look and propose if they want a formal invoice adjustment or a policy update to attribution. I'll keep this thread updated. Thanks all for the quick turn. :rocket:
